Subject: Observability + SDK/Auth follow-up — SDK setup, routing, and latency headers

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the FintechCo infra and product teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Primary integration patterns we discussed: SDK/server-to-server API (preferred), and a short client-forwarding option for low-sensitivity features.
- Auth options: you mentioned OIDC as preferred; noted SAML for SSO-based workflows. We can support both (see attached sdk-oidc-setup.md).
- Routing & model variants: recommended routing by endpoint tag (e.g., /v1/generate?route=low-latency or route=cost-optimized). We can automatically fallback to a compatible model variant on capacity constraints.
- Structured output & tool-calling: Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs; we can add a strict schema for transaction parsing.
- Embeddings / reranker flow: for search relevance you wanted dense embeddings + a lightweight reranker to re-score top-k. We'll surface embedding vector IDs and the reranker score in the response; see fields below.
- Observability: you asked for trace IDs, logging fields, and latency breakdown headers. Rishi (cc'd) will provide concrete header/field names and an example SDK snippet.

Next steps:
1) Rishi to send header names, logging fields, and example SDK code for OIDC.
2) FintechCo infra to confirm OIDC provider & token exchange flow (client credentials vs on-behalf-of).
3) Schedule a follow-up call with infra engineers — propose Thu 7/2 at 10am PT.

Attachments: integration-playbook.pdf (quick stub)

Let me know if I captured anything incorrectly.

—

Subject: Re: Observability + SDK/Auth follow-up — SDK setup, routing, and latency headers

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Below are the recommended header names, logging fields, example SDK snippets (server-side), and dashboard suggestions. Happy to walk through these on the follow-up call.

1) Trace / request id
- Header: X-Request-Id (client-generated if available) — Redwood will echo and persist as rdw.request_id.
- Server-assigned: X-Rdw-Trace-Id — Redwood will always set this if X-Request-Id is missing. Use either one as the canonical trace id.

2) Latency breakdown headers (per-response)
- X-Rdw-Latency-Total-ms: total server-side latency in ms
- X-Rdw-Latency-Gen-ms: model generation time (token decode/compute)
- X-Rdw-Latency-KV-ms: KV/prefix cache time
- X-Rdw-Latency-Batching-ms: batching/queueing time
- X-Rdw-Latency-Network-ms: server egress network time (if applicable)

We also include X-Rdw-Model and X-Rdw-Model-Version for quick routing visibility.

3) Logging fields (structured log JSON line you can ingest)
- rdw.request_id: string
- rdw.trace_id: string
- rdw.model: model_name
- rdw.model_version: version
- rdw.seq_len: request_sequence_length
- rdw.tokens_generated: integer
- rdw.latency_total_ms: integer
- rdw.latency_gen_ms: integer
- rdw.latency_kv_ms: integer
- rdw.latency_batch_ms: integer
- rdw.reranker_score: float (when reranker used)
- rdw.embedding_id: string (when embeddings returned)

Example log line (single-line JSON):
{"rdw.request_id":"b7f3c2a8-9d3e-4c2b-8a1f-123456789abc", "rdw.model":"redwood-llama-3-7b", "rdw.latency_total_ms":153, "rdw.latency_gen_ms":120, "rdw.latency_kv_ms":12, "rdw.latency_batch_ms":18, "rdw.reranker_score":0.82}

4) Sample SDK curl (server-to-server, client credentials/OIDC flow)
- Exchange client credentials for token at your IdP; include Bearer token in Authorization header.

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"input":"Summarize transaction 0x...","options":{"route":"low-latency"}}'

Python (requests):
import requests
import uuid
headers = {
  "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['REDWOOD_TOKEN']}",
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  "X-Request-Id": str(uuid.uuid4())
}
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate", json={"input":"...","options":{"route":"low-latency"}}, headers=headers)
# Read latency headers
lat_total = resp.headers.get('X-Rdw-Latency-Total-ms')
lat_gen = resp.headers.get('X-Rdw-Latency-Gen-ms')

5) Embeddings / reranker fields in response
- embeddings: [ {"embedding_id": "vec_abc123", "vector": [...], "score": 0.0 } ] (we typically omit the full vector when returning to clients; vector id and metadata are included)
- reranker: {"reranker_score":0.82, "reranker_model":"redwood-rerank-1"}

6) Dashboard / Datadog panels suggestions
- Service map: model name + average latency_total_ms
- Top N endpoints by error rate and p95 latency
- Latency breakdown chart (stacked): gen vs kv vs batch vs network
- Trace sampling: include rdw.request_id as trace attribute for correlation

Attachments: observability-headers.md, sdk-oidc-setup.md (stubs attached to this thread).

If you want, we can provide a short webhook that forwards these headers into your Datadog ingest or a minimal Fluent Bit config to parse the rdw.* fields.

Happy to iterate — we can also include a small eval harness to show p50/p95 changes when enabling prefix caching and reranker.
